_note: Real Urban Sports Club partner venues in Berlin. Names, addresses, activities, opening hours, the per-plan visit limits, the latitude/longitude and the photographs all come from the public venue pages on urbansportsclub.com — each venue's `url` links to its source page. The first 15 venues were retrieved 12 August 2026, the next 31 on 19 August 2026, and a further 147 were retrieved on 19 August 2026 in a second pass, for 193 venues in total; every venue's coordinates come from a retrieval on 19 August 2026. Coordinates are the `geo` values published on each page, not approximations, so distances are real rather than indicative. Most of the second-pass venues carry no `blurb` and no `goodToKnow`: their published descriptions are German marketing prose, and rather than translate that into claims we cannot check, those fields are left null — 46 of 193 venues have a blurb. Access strings are the published allowances in the venue's own words, so two phrasings that did not appear before now do: "1 visit a month" and "2 visits a month". Three things are NOT published by the source: `tier`/`tierLabel`, which is inferred from the four-plan access table (Essential included → standard, otherwise Classic included → plus, otherwise premium) and is not a label the venue pages carry; the Charlottenburg area centroid, which is derived as the mean of the published coordinates of the six Charlottenburg venues from the first import (the other area centroids are approximate district reference points); and the short `blurb`/`goodToKnow` lines that are present, which are written from each page rather than copied. Each venue's `area` is assigned by nearest area centroid using its published coordinates, which is how the app measures distance too; the single exception is `k4-athletics`, which sits about 70 m nearer the Mitte centroid but keeps the Friedrichshain area it was first given. Photos load from Urban Sports Club's own media bucket, so they need an internet connection; offline, each card falls back to a branded icon tile. Three venues also carry an inlined photograph from the supplied designs as an offline fallback, so the demo still shows photography with no network at all.
